title: 1961 AHSME Problem 33
statement: The number of solutions of \(2^{2x}-3^{2y}=55,\) in which \(x\) and \(y\) are integers, is:

solutions.text:
Factor: \[ (2^x-3^y)(2^x+3^y)=55. \] First, \(x>0.\) If \(y\le0,\) then \(55<4^x\le56,\) which is impossible for an integral power of \(4.\) Hence \(y>0,\) so both factors are positive odd integers. The factor pair \(5,\) \(11\) gives \(2^{x+1}=16\) and \(2\cdot3^y=6,\) so \((x,y)=(3,1).\) The factor pair \(1,\) \(55\) would require \(2^x=28,\) impossible. Hence there is exactly one solution.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Factor the left side as a difference of squares
The two positive factors multiply to \(55\) and have the same parity
